trust_decision.summary: A caller-supplied (or server-stored) GridFS file id of type Bson is put directly as the value of `_id` / `files_id` in a server-side filter, so a document id like {$gt: MinKey} is read by the server as a query operator instead of a literal; the driver decides 'literal match only' by wrapping the value in $eq at each filter construction site.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'disclosure and deletion via ... file IDs'; GridFsBucket::delete(id: Bson) (driver/src/action/gridfs/delete.rs:17) and open_download_stream(id) (driver/src/action/gridfs/download.rs:20) are the obvious id-taking public APIs in the action/gridfs module.

fix_sites.entry_point: GridFsDownloadStream::new, reached from open_download_stream (driver/src/action/gridfs/download.rs:144) and open_download_stream_by_name (driver/src/action/gridfs/download.rs:171) with file.id read back from the files collection

clean_up_chunks, reached from GridFsUploadStream::abort (driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:257), poll_close while writing (driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:350), write_bytes insert failure (driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:407), close insert failure (driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:438); id set by OpenUploadStream::id (driver/src/action/gridfs/upload.rs:57)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: driver/src/gridfs/download.rs:95 reached from open_download_stream_by_name (driver/src/action/gridfs/download.rs:166-171): the files_id filter uses file.id deserialized from the stored FilesCollectionDocument (driver/src/gridfs.rs:47-50), an id that was stored earlier via the upload stream with a caller-chosen id (driver/src/action/gridfs/upload.rs:57, driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:431). Secondary: upload abort/cleanup path driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:447, which does not look like an id lookup at all.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Download-by-name never takes an id from the caller and the id comes from the server's own files document, so a solver can say it is 'trusted data'; the upload abort/cleanup path deletes 'our own' chunks for a stream the caller just opened, so it does not look like a lookup by an untrusted id.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: GridFS file ids are arbitrary Bson, including documents, and stay legitimate (compound or document ids must still download, rename and delete by exact match). Also, GridFsBucket::find/find_one take a raw user filter Document by design, and find_file_by_id itself goes through self.find_one. A fix that rejects document-typed ids or $-prefixed keys, or that sanitizes find/find_one filters, breaks legitimate use.

O6_input_shapes: id given as a Bson document whose top-level key is a query operator (e.g. {$gt: MinKey}) passed to delete/rename/open_download_stream (fix.diff:79-113)
the same operator-shaped id stored as a file's _id via open_upload_stream().id() and later used as file.id from the stored document (fix.diff:125-126)
the same operator-shaped id held by an upload stream and used in abort/error cleanup (fix.diff:147-148)

O7_producer.where: driver/src/gridfs.rs:47-50 (FilesCollectionDocument.id: Bson, deserialized from the files collection in find_file_by_name, driver/src/action/gridfs/download.rs:72-79)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Upload stream Drop handler (stream dropped without abort/close, including the sync GridFsUploadStream wrapper which owns the async stream) spawns chunks.delete_many with an unwrapped files_id filter; the published fix changed clean_up_chunks but not this inline duplicate.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fire-and-forget best-effort cleanup in Drop whose result is discarded (`let _result`), and docs tell users to prefer abort (driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:154-157), so a solver can call it a non-API background path, or assume it already routes through clean_up_chunks.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the clean_up_chunks fix site (driver/src/gridfs/upload.rs:447), different module from the landing point (driver/src/action/gridfs/delete.rs)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: delete_by_name currently gathers server-stored ids and uses $in (literal per element). A variant that loops and deletes chunks per stored id with {files_id: id} would be a stored-id sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A per-file loop is a natural rewrite (e.g. for per-file error reporting), and the ids come from the server so a maintainer would see them as trusted.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A seek/resume or retry-after-cursor-error path in GridFsDownloadStream that re-queries chunks with {files_id: file.id, n: {$gte: k}}
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Resuming a chunk cursor after a transient error is a plausible feature and would rebuild the filter from stored file.id away from the patched constructor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An upload 'overwrite/replace existing id' option that first deletes existing files/chunks matching the caller-chosen id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Replace-on-upload is a common GridFS convenience in other drivers and would add a delete keyed on the caller id inside upload machinery.

O9_family: NoSQL query-operator injection (CWE-943) via Bson document values in filter positions

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Wrap the id in $eq only in delete/rename/open_download_stream in action/gridfs, or reject document-typed or $-keyed ids up front, missing the stored-id and upload-cleanup/Drop paths or breaking legitimate document ids.
